title: How to blur background in Zoom on Mac: step by step for Zoom Workplace
metaTitle: How to Blur Background in Zoom on Mac, Step by Step
description: How to blur background in Zoom on Mac: exact menu paths for Zoom Workplace, before or during a meeting, plus fixes for when Blur is missing.
targetKeyword: how to blur background in zoom on mac
intro: To blur background in Zoom on Mac, open the Zoom Workplace desktop app, click your profile picture, and choose Settings > Video & effects > Virtual backgrounds > Blur. During a meeting, click the arrow next to Video, choose Video & effect settings, and click Blur there.
tldr: Before a meeting: profile picture > Settings > Video & effects > Virtual backgrounds > Blur.
During a meeting: the arrow next to Video > Video & effect settings > Virtual backgrounds > Blur.
Blur lives in the Zoom Workplace desktop app. The web app only offers Choose Background.
If Blur is missing, check your app version, your macOS version and your Mac's chip.
Zoom's Mac shortcuts cover video and audio. None covers Settings or Virtual backgrounds.

blocks.text: Why Blur sits under Virtual backgrounds

Zoom does not put Blur on the main toolbar. Blur is one of the virtual background choices, next to the image and video options. That is why the path runs through Settings or the Video & effects panel, then the Virtual backgrounds tab. Blur keeps you in focus and softens the room behind you.
Use the desktop app, not the web app

Zoom's support article describes two routes, and only one has Blur. The desktop app has it. The web app does not. In the web client, you join or start a meeting, click the up arrow next to Start/Stop Video, and click Choose Background. Those steps only cover background images and your own uploads.

If you cannot add an image in the web client, Zoom says to contact your Zoom admin. Zoom's current system requirements article calls the desktop app Zoom Workplace. Older third-party guides say Zoom or Zoom Desktop Client. The article does not explain the name change, so use the name you see on your screen when you follow these steps.
What your Mac needs for blur to work

Blur is a virtual background, so it has conditions. Zoom lists three. Your device must meet the system requirements. The Virtual background setting must be enabled. The desktop app must be at or above the global minimum version. Here is what those conditions mean on a Mac.

items: macOS 10.15 or later for the Zoom desktop app. Zoom's system requirements article says client 7.0.0 dropped macOS 10.13 and 10.14.
Apple silicon, or an Intel i5 (5th gen) or higher, for image backgrounds without a green screen.
A 720p cap on your outgoing video when you use a virtual background without a green screen.
Background video at 1080p needs more hardware. Zoom lists Apple M-series MacBook Pro for that tier without a green screen.
The Virtual background setting enabled. If it is off, ask your Zoom admin.

blocks.text: Check your chip and macOS version through the Apple menu > About This Mac. Compare what you see with the list above. A Mac that falls below these lines may not show Blur, even when you follow the menu path correctly.
Check the Zoom version when Blur is missing

The version check is the step people skip. Zoom's minimum version article defines the minimum as the absolute minimum app version you can use to join or host a Zoom Meeting. Below that version, you must update before you sign in or join. Users who cannot update right away can join through the web app, but the web app has no Blur option.

blocks.caption: Zoom's macOS version targets for the desktop app

blocks.text: Zoom publishes a slow track and a fast track. The article gives 7.2.5 as the fast-track version as of 10/31/26. If your Blur option is missing, update the app until it reaches at least that number. Zoom changes these numbers over time, so check the article again before you rely on an older date.
Turn on Blur during a meeting

You do not have to leave the call to change your background. In the meeting controls, click the arrow next to Video. Then click Video & effect settings. The Video & effects side panel opens. Click the Virtual backgrounds tab, or scroll down to it below the preview, and click Blur.
Zoom's instructions say the change applies immediately when video is on. If your video is off, turn it on first. Watch the preview in the side panel to confirm the blur before you start talking.
Keyboard shortcuts on a Mac during a call

Zoom's Mac hot-key article lists shortcuts for the basics of a meeting. ⌘⇧V starts and stops video. ⌘⇧A mutes and unmutes audio. Hold the Space bar to unmute for a moment. If you are the host, ⌘⌃M mutes everyone except the host, and ⌘⌃U unmutes everyone except the host.
The article lists no shortcut for Settings or Virtual backgrounds. Plan on the mouse for Blur. Use the keys for the video and audio you need during the call, and let the mouse handle the background.
Blur or an image: what a 2024 study found

A 2024 study in Frontiers in Psychology looked at 610 videoconference users in Singapore. It found that 443 of them, or 72.6%, used some kind of virtual background. Of those users, 162 (26.6%) chose a blurred background, 223 (36.6%) chose an image, and 58 (9.5%) chose a video background. The other 167 users, or 27.4%, used none.

The same study measured videoconference fatigue. Mean scores were 3.44 for video backgrounds, 2.85 for blurred backgrounds and 2.65 for image backgrounds. A Kruskal-Wallis test showed a difference across the three groups, with p below 0.001.

Read these numbers as a pattern, not a rule. A study of this type shows what people chose and how they scored. It does not show that blur causes less fatigue. Pick Blur because it hides a messy room, and treat the study as background reading.
Common mistakes that make Blur disappear

items: Using the web app. Its steps only offer Choose Background, with images or uploads.
Following an old guide. Third-party guides that cite client 5.5.0 and older Intel tiers conflict with Zoom's current pages.
Changing the background with video off. The change applies right away only when video is on.
Skipping the update. An app below the minimum version has to update before it can join.
Assuming any Mac can do it all. Image backgrounds without a green screen need Apple silicon or an Intel i5 (5th gen) or higher.
Expecting sharp 1080p everywhere. Without a green screen, your outgoing video is capped at 720p.

blocks.text: Fixing Blur when it is greyed out

Work down the list in order. Start with the app. Confirm you are in the Zoom Workplace desktop app, not a browser tab. Next, compare your version with the table above. Then check the Mac. Confirm macOS 10.15 or later, and confirm the chip meets the image background tier.

If everything matches and Blur still does not appear, the account setting is the likely cause. Zoom's requirements say the Virtual background setting must be enabled. Ask your admin to check it. Zoom's guidance for a missing background option is to contact your Zoom admin.
Edge cases before an important call

Blur only changes the background. It does not fix poor light, a noisy room or a weak connection. Put a clear gap between you and the wall, and face a light source. Those habits matter more than the setting.

Also watch the video quality. Without a green screen, Zoom caps outgoing video at 720p when you use a virtual background. If a call needs sharper video, such as a live demo, test the setup with a colleague before you rely on it. The cap is tied to having no green screen.
Next steps after you turn on Blur

Once Blur is on, check how you look in the preview, then join a test meeting if the call matters. If you would rather show a picture behind you, read [how to change your virtual background in Zoom on Mac](/how-to/change-your-virtual-background-in-zoom).

If your next step is sharing your screen, the camera and screen share steps are separate. Start with [camera access in Zoom on Mac](/how-to/grant-camera-access-in-zoom) if your camera is blocked. For a black preview on a share, read [how to fix black screen share in Zoom on Mac](/how-to/fix-a-black-screen-share-in-zoom).

faq.question: Is Blur the same thing as a virtual background in Zoom?
faq.answer: Blur is one of Zoom's virtual background choices. It sits in the same Virtual backgrounds tab as the images. Instead of a picture, it softens what is behind you.

faq.question: Can I blur my background in the Zoom web app on Mac?
faq.answer: Not with a Blur option. Zoom's web steps cover Choose Background, which lets you pick an image or upload your own. Use the Zoom Workplace desktop app for blur.

faq.question: Why does Blur not show up in Zoom on my Mac?
faq.answer: The usual causes are an app below Zoom's minimum version, the web client, or a Mac that misses the chip or macOS requirement. Check the app version first, then confirm macOS 10.15 or later.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to turn on Blur?
faq.answer: No. Zoom's Mac hot-key article lists no shortcut for Settings or Virtual backgrounds. ⌘⇧V starts and stops video, and video needs to be on for the change to apply right away.

faq.question: Does a blurred background lower video quality?
faq.answer: Blur is a virtual background, and without a green screen Zoom caps outgoing video at 720p. The cap applies only when you have no green screen. If you need sharper video, test the setup before a call that matters.

faq.question: Does a blurred background reduce video call fatigue?
faq.answer: A 2024 study of 610 users found mean fatigue of 2.85 for blurred backgrounds, 2.65 for image backgrounds and 3.44 for video backgrounds. It shows an association in one sample. It does not prove that blur causes less fatigue.

faq.question: What if my admin turned virtual backgrounds off?
faq.answer: Zoom's requirements list an enabled Virtual background setting as a condition. If you cannot add a background, Zoom's guidance is to contact your Zoom admin.

task: Blur your background in Zoom on Mac
appliesTo: Zoom Workplace desktop app on macOS 10.15 or later
requirements: Zoom Workplace desktop app, not the web client
Apple silicon, or an Intel i5 (5th gen) or higher, for image backgrounds without a green screen
Desktop app at or above Zoom's global minimum version
Virtual background setting enabled for your account

steps.name: Open the Zoom Workplace desktop app
steps.text: Open Zoom Workplace on your Mac and sign in. Launch it from Applications or the Dock. Do not use a browser tab, because the web client has no Blur option.
steps.tip: If you are already in a meeting, skip to the during-meeting steps below.

steps.name: Click your profile picture
steps.text: Look at the top-right corner of the Zoom window. Click your profile picture to open the account menu.

steps.name: Open Settings
steps.text: In the account menu, click Settings. The Settings window opens with its list of tabs.

steps.name: Open the Video & effects tab
steps.text: In Settings, click the Video & effects tab. This is where your camera preview and background options live.

steps.name: Open the Virtual backgrounds tab
steps.text: Click the Virtual backgrounds tab. Blur is one of the choices here, next to your background images.

steps.name: Click Blur
steps.text: Click Blur. Turn your video on if you want to see the effect in the preview before you join a meeting.
steps.tip: If Blur is missing or greyed out, check the version and requirements before you go further.

steps.name: Click the arrow next to Video
steps.text: During a meeting, find Video in the meeting controls toolbar. Click the small arrow beside it to open the camera menu.

steps.name: Click Video & effect settings
steps.text: In the camera menu, click Video & effect settings. The Video & effects side panel opens with a preview of your camera.

steps.name: Open Virtual backgrounds in the panel
steps.text: Click the Virtual backgrounds tab in the side panel, or scroll down to it below the preview.

steps.name: Click Blur and check the preview
steps.text: Click Blur. If your video is on, the change applies immediately. Look at your preview to confirm, then close the panel when you are happy with it.
steps.tip: If your camera is off, start video with ⌘⇧V first, then check the preview.

troubleshooting.problem: Blur is missing or greyed out
troubleshooting.fix: Update Zoom Workplace first. Zoom lists 6.0.2 as the macOS minimum and 7.2.5 as the fast-track version as of 10/31/26. Below the minimum, the app asks you to update before you can join.

troubleshooting.problem: You are using the web app
troubleshooting.fix: Switch to the Zoom Workplace desktop app. The web client only offers Choose Background, and it does not list a Blur option.

troubleshooting.problem: Blur does not show during the call
troubleshooting.fix: Turn video on. Zoom says the change applies immediately when video is on. Then check the preview in the Video & effects side panel.

troubleshooting.problem: Your Mac is older than the requirements
troubleshooting.fix: Check the chip and macOS version in About This Mac. Zoom requires macOS 10.15 or later for the app. Image backgrounds without a green screen need Apple silicon or an Intel i5 (5th gen) or higher.

troubleshooting.problem: Video looks soft after you add a background
troubleshooting.fix: Without a green screen, Zoom caps outgoing video at 720p when you use a virtual background. Test the setup before an important call, because the cap is tied to having no green screen.

troubleshooting.problem: You cannot add a background at all
troubleshooting.fix: Ask your Zoom admin. Zoom's guidance says to contact your admin when you cannot add a background, and the Virtual background setting must be enabled.
